caption: The drawing shows a rectangular garden layout with a beige background and a black outline fence surrounding the garden area. At the top center, the text "SPERRY'S VAUXHALL GARDEN" appears in red capital letters, with faint floral line art in light brown extending from both top corners. The interior of the garden is primarily filled with a textured green surface, representing grass or lawn. There are seven rectangular garden beds or plots rendered in reddish-brown and arranged in a formal, grid-like pattern. Each bed contains small green circular shapes suggesting plants or bushes, with some beds having a larger green circle at their center. Along the right side, a vertical line of six standalone green circular shapes appears, possibly indicating larger bushes or trees. Near the bottom center-left, there is a small building with a white base and red roof, and an adjacent white archway. Leading from the archway are two curved green pathways or hedges that branch outwards, one straight towards a greenhouse-like structure positioned just above the house, with a peaked roof shaded in light greens. The entire composition is formally arranged and uses muted, natural tones of green, brown, and beige, with highlighted accents in red and white.
title: Sperry Gardens
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
